newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ex-movie star leader released on bail.
newsitem.headline: India's ex-movie star leader released on bail.

text.p: India's best-known woman politician and former movie star left prison on Friday after being granted bail on corruption charges, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
Jayaraman Jayalalitha, who ruled the southern state of Tamil Nadu for five years until last year, spent 28 days behind bars while fighting for bail.
She was arrested on December 7 by police who accused her of excess spending in the government purchase of television sets for villages in her state while she was chief minister.

Jayalalitha, leader of the regional All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) party, has denied charges and has accused her successor government of the rival Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party of revenge in launching investigations.
Police raided two of her homes and said they recovered hundreds of pairs of shoes, expensive jewellery and other items worth more than 580 million rupees ($16 million).

She has been accused of misusing public office for personal gains in the import of coal from Australia by the state-run electricity board and of possessing assets disproportionate to her known sources of income.
Jayalalitha quit films in 1982 after a successful acting career to become one of India's most powerful regional politicians.
She took over the AIADMK, a party representing low-caste Hindus and Tamil speakers, from her former co-star and mentor, matinee idol M.G. Ramachandran, after his death in 1987.
